findings.title: Preserve receipt deduplication across ledger rotation and retry
findings.scenario: An append reaches disk but fails before acknowledgement (for example fsync/revalidation failure). The original account retains that receipt and gains a second receipt. At the active-segment capacity boundary, the retry rotates the first receipt into the archive and then appends the entire pending batch to the new segment.
evidence: flush_rows_once checks receipt identities only in the active segment; matching rows are skipped but not removed from pending before the next rotation pass.
flush_rows invokes its final Append pass with the original pending slice after rotate archived the already-written receipt. The fresh active segment has no identity for it.

Root executed rereview_retry_across_rotation_counts_receipt_once against HEAD: expected two session receipts, observed three. Probe uses one valid persisted row plus that same unacknowledged pending row and one fresh row; it does not require an invalid ledger.
findings.fix: Retain durable deduplication across generation changes, including retries after another writer rotates. Do not acknowledge a receipt before its durable state is established; do not rely only on the new segment identity map.
acceptance_tests: Regression reproduces a complete persisted but unacknowledged receipt at rotation and proves all-time/session/model tokens and cost count it exactly once.
Cover mixed old/new pending batches in both iteration orders, a concurrent second writer rotating before retry, and conflicting receipt identities across retained segments.
Existing rotation, crash recovery, and idempotent-save tests keep passing.
findings.validation: Root Rust negative-control test failed as expected: session.records=3, expected2. See ledger-probes.log and ledger-probes.rs.

findings.title: Recover archived session totals when the rollup detail cap omits a session
findings.scenario: After archived history spans more than4096 distinct sessions, RollupState drops later session details. Startup reconciliation of a dropped session still succeeds with zero archived session usage. A rollup exceeding16MiB similarly discards all per-session details.
evidence: RollupState::add sets sessions_dropped when the4096-session map fills; store_rollup can also serialize an empty session map to fit the16MiB cap.
RollupState::apply only merges sessions.get(id) and never checks sessions_dropped or scans archived receipts for a missing session.

startup.rs1645 passes the incomplete summary.session into Account::reconcile, which marks ledger_ready and uses its token/cost totals. Saved legacy cost can preserve previously saved monetary estimates, but cannot recover charges after the last save; session token reconciliation also loses omitted archived usage.
Root probe writes a valid archive containing4097 distinct sessions and calls session_summary for the last: it returns0 records although that session has one receipt.
findings.fix: Treat omitted session detail as incomplete. Recover the requested session from archives or maintain a bounded exact lookup; otherwise fail closed for admission rather than returning an exact-looking zero.
acceptance_tests: With4097 sessions across rotated segments, both session_summary and summary_for_session recover the last session's exact tokens/cost or explicitly refuse incomplete accounting.
Exercise rollup size fallback and a requested session with both archived and active receipts.
A resumed session with a token or USD cap cannot admit work using silently omitted archived charges; retain the monotonic saved-estimate behavior.
findings.validation: Root Rust negative-control test failed as expected: session.records=0, expected1. See ledger-probes.log and ledger-probes.rs.

findings.title: Real token-pressure relief can be skipped and then falsely classified as irreducible context
findings.scenario: Configure mid_turn_compact_threshold=0.80 and a 100k context window with a 10k reserve. A tool-bearing completion reports 81k real prompt tokens, while the local session estimate stays below the normal 90k between-turn budget and has a legal old prefix. The real-pressure boundary requests compaction. compact_and_respawn(Some(.81)) passes force=false, and the inner planner returns WithinBudget because byte pressure is false and local tokens<=90k. No summarizer runs. The app nonetheless marks awaiting_compaction_relief=true. On the next completion still above .80 it stops with StopContextExhausted and claims compaction ran/the floor is irreducible, despite never trying the available legal cut.
evidence: App::handle_agent_event derives mid_turn_pressure from provider usage divided by context_window and the configured threshold (app.rs4773-4801).
compact_and_respawn passes pressure.is_none() as force; all ordinary token and byte boundaries carry Some(pressure), so their force=false (ui/mod.rs1919-1927).

handle_compress_unfloored passes auto&&!force and byte_pressure into plan_tui_compaction (slash/mod.rs553-560). The planner still skips below its independent window-minus-reserve token budget if no byte pressure (803-809).

App sets awaiting_compaction_relief=true after the handler regardless of whether any compaction occurred (app.rs4918). mid_turn_pressure_action returns StopContextExhausted when awaiting and still over threshold (app.rs820-833); stop text says compaction ran (ui/mod.rs2039 onward).

This differs from fixed xorxl.6: actionable byte pressure now bypasses the local gate correctly, but real token pressure still does not. Headless relief force-compacts on measured pressure and does not make this token-gate assumption.
regression_tests: Review-only pure-function control proves a legal old cut with force and an ordinary WithinBudget result without real pressure; negative probe applies the actual compact_and_respawn argument choices for Some(.81) and expects a Cut. Root can append the provided module to slash/mod.rs and run filter rereview_token_boundary.

Final production regression should drive actual App token-pressure boundary at threshold0.80 while local count<window-reserve; assert summarizer receives the old prefix and the following prompt continues below threshold rather than stopping as irreducible.
Add no-old-prefix and summarizer-failure cases: do not mark compaction successfully performed when it did not occur, and preserve already completed effects.
findings.validation: Root executed corrected review-only probes: control PASS (legal old compaction cut exists and ordinary auto remains WithinBudget), regression FAIL with WithinBudget when actual real-pressure caller arguments should reach that cut. Log /private/tmp/mini-agent-rereview-final-probes.log. Initial control fixture mistake was corrected before this accepted result. This agent ran no Cargo.

findings.title: A SubagentStop hook grants fresh exploration turns after the child max_turns budget is exhausted
findings.scenario: Enable hooks and configure a global SubagentStop hook that returns a block/continue reason. Set task max_turns=1. A child uses its one allowed turn on a tool call and returns Ok(partial: turn budget exhausted). Because the branch checks only task weighted units and response Ok, the stop hook requests continuation. task_tool then starts a fresh run_subagent with max_turns=1 again, permitting another exploration/tool round. A successful child that used any smaller positive portion of the cap also receives the full cap rather than the remainder.
evidence: SUBAGENTS.md169 defines max_turns as the child model-turn budget; table1240 calls it max agent turns per subagent;1545 defines exhausted turn budget as an Ok partial result. New child relief comment task_tool.rs4247 explicitly states max_turns bounds the whole task.
run_subagent_with_history maps MaxTurnsError to turn_budget_exhausted=true and Ok partial response (runner.rs6260 onward), so budget exhaustion does not exclude the hook branch.

Global SubagentStop Decision::Block maps to SubagentStopGate::Continue at hooks/mod.rs964. task_tool.rs2222-2230 checks only !task_budget.exhausted() and Ok response, then run_subagent(...max_turns...) at2234-2242 restarts the full exploration allowance.

merge_forced_continuation_run sums the extra turns after they have occurred; it does not enforce the cap. This is an exploration-cap bypass, separate from the deliberate one-turn tool-free summary/write-up/repair exceptions.

Outer bounds still apply: LiveTaskBudget tracks weighted units (task_tool.rs1869,1900-1915,1955) and the scheduler whole-call deadline (3505,3540 onward) includes the branch. Defaults4m units and300s do not stop two quick low-token requests, so they do not enforce the independent max_turns=1 contract. This is at most one extra full exploration segment, not an unbounded loop.
regression_tests: Use actual task tool execution with hooks enabled and a global SubagentStop Block hook, max_turns=1, large weighted-unit budget, and generous deadline. Script a tool-bearing first completion followed by a second tool-bearing completion; assert the second provider exploration request/tool never executes.

With max_turns=3 and two initial exploration completions, a forced continuation may get at most one remaining turn. Assert total exploration turns in ChildDetails never exceed3 and already completed tool effects/evidence remain retained.
Keep tool-free report repair/write-up separately bounded as documented; retain existing weighted-unit and whole-call timeout protections.

findings.title: Initial Gemini command credentials still bypass query encoding and can lose renewal ownership
findings.origin: Adjacent remaining defect; predates this corrective diff. This is not a regression introduced by the xorxl.9 fix.
findings.scenario: A custom Gemini-compatible gateway uses a command-issued token containing a reserved query character. These characters are accepted by credential_from_output and are explicitly covered by the existing reserved-character encoding contract. The SDK constructs its initial request using that token directly in the key query field.
evidence: GeminiExt::build_uri formats self.api_key directly into the URL for both normal and streaming requests; it does not encode the query value.

CommandCredential::apply rewrites a query only when candidates does not contain current. Therefore a current construction-time token with a plus sign bypasses with_query_key and remains raw on the wire, where normal query decoding changes its value.

An ampersand in that initial token is worse: query_key splits the raw query at ampersands, so ownership sees only a prefix; apply returns None and the request loses the credential renewal/resend path as well as transmitting the wrong token.

query_key_rewrite_percent_encodes_reserved_characters tests with_query_key directly. gemini_query_string_key_is_refreshed_and_renewed_on_401 uses safe construction/rotation tokens, so neither exercises the initial SDK-built reserved-character token.
findings.mitigation: Encode the credential when the SDK initially builds the URL, or use Gemini header authentication so the full original token is never parsed out of an already ambiguous raw query. Canonicalizing only stale query credentials is insufficient.
regression_test_acceptance: Construct an actual custom Gemini SDK client once with a command helper whose first token contains reserved query characters; loopback assertions verify that both streaming and non-streaming requests contain exactly the original token after normal query decoding, with no unintended parameters.
Include initial plus, ampersand, percent, hash and space cases. Exercise a 401 followed by rotation and prove ownership/renewal remains attached.
Preserve the existing multi-rotation coverage and confirm safe tokens and unrelated query parameters remain unchanged.
findings.validation: Static call-path and indexed implementation review. No credential command, live provider request, exploit, or new proof-of-concept was executed.
findings.root_verification: Root also executed two synthetic initial-token probes: raw plus remained unencoded; ampersand lost renewal ownership. No real credentials or external requests used.

findings.title: Keep MCP cancellation and EOF handling live while stdout is backpressured
findings.scenario: Start a silent long-running run, then let a ping/finished-run reply fill the MCP stdout pipe while the client stops reading. Close stdin or send notifications/cancelled. The dispatch task is stuck awaiting write_message and cannot receive the queued EOF/cancel; active model/tool work keeps running until its independent run timeout. The new EOF branch can also block flushing queued replies before the cancellation teardown.
evidence: serve awaits write_message inside its dispatch select arms (1127,1169); write_message uses unbounded output.write_all and flush awaits at1193-1194. The reader task can enqueue EOF/cancel, but the dispatch task cannot poll line_rx while blocked in a write.

The new EOF handler itself flushes all reply_rx entries through the same unbounded await before return (1081-1082). Active runs are cancelled only after this enclosing async block returns, at1179-1182.
The new stdin_eof_retires_a_silent_running_call_and_its_process_group test keeps stdout empty, so it proves idle EOF but not EOF/cancellation during a response write.

A deterministic source-level probe for the existing tests module is saved at /private/tmp/mini-agent-rereview-mcp-backpressure-probe.rs. It uses a one-byte output duplex, starts the existing shell fixture, confirms a ping response entered write_message by reading its first byte, then leaves stdout unread and closes stdin. Root may run it with coordinated Cargo; no Rust probe execution is claimed by this subagent.

Root independently executed the supplied current-source backpressure regression probe and observed retired=false, child_live=true; the blocked server was then aborted for cleanup. This confirms the concrete failure, beyond static path analysis.
findings.fix: Decouple/bound the output writer so transport retirement and notifications/cancelled can run while output is stalled; cancel and join active runs before any EOF reply drain, and bound that drain.
acceptance_tests: Run the supplied fixture and assert EOF retires serve and the whole child tree despite an open, unread stdout stream. Repeat using notifications/cancelled while a reply is blocked, and cover a large completed reply queued alongside an active run.
findings.validation: Root independently reproduced: retired=false child_live=true; cleanup completed.

findings.title: Own Windows helper and run descendants instead of killing only the direct process
findings.scenario: On Windows, an opted-in unsandboxed headersHelper launches a credential subprocess and waits. Cancel the MCP connect/reconnect or let the helper time out. The helper is killed, but the subprocess survives. The MCP server run process has the same direct-child-only ownership when a run is cancelled/retired.
evidence: The new GroupKillOnDrop has an empty Drop implementation outside Unix: its only action is under #[cfg(unix)] at headers_helper.rs87-90. command.process_group(0) is Unix-only too.

An unsandboxed helper comes from stdio_command as a plain tokio Command (client.rs1612-1618), then uses .kill_on_drop(true) and spawn_guarded (headers_helper.rs127-131). process_creation::spawn_tokio_once and TokioCommandCreationExt only acquire the creation lock and call TokioCommand::spawn; they never attach a Job Object.
The ordinary helper timeout/completion cleanup uses child.start_kill on non-Unix at headers_helper.rs156-158, so even waiting for the internal deadline does not terminate descendants.

server.rs run_prompt likewise launches a plain tokio Child with kill_on_drop, and its group guard is Unix-only. kill_tree on non-Unix calls only child.start_kill. Thus the new EOF teardown does not establish descendant retirement on Windows.

The repository already has owned_workspace_service_tree in sandbox.rs834-841, which wraps Windows workspace services in JobObject; these two paths bypass it. All new helper and MCP EOF fixtures are cfg(unix), leaving the platform branch unproved.
findings.fix: Use a Windows kill-on-close Job/owned process-tree wrapper for the helper and the MCP server run, retained through normal completion, timeout, cancellation and future drop. Preserve the Unix group guard.
acceptance_tests: On native Windows, have a helper and an MCP run each start a child that records its pid, then test cancellation, EOF, timeout and dropped-future paths; both the direct and descendant processes must be gone. Test the default unsandboxed trusted helper path.
findings.limitation: No native Windows execution performed; the missing Job ownership and cfg branches are directly visible.

findings.title: Parse raw aliases separately from encoded IDs in the ACP /model command
findings.scenario: Configure a quick-model alias named alias:fast. /model lists that raw name and advertises /model [alias|default], but typing /model alias:fast now fails because the wire decoder strips the prefix. If both default and alias:default exist, typing the displayed alias:default instead selects the default alias/provider.
evidence: The new parse_model correctly strips exactly one reserved prefix and validates the canonical wire encoding (134-135), making the selector IDs injective.

The slash command passes its raw argument directly to set_model_override at acp/mod.rs4077, which calls the same parse_model at2213; no encoding step distinguishes literal command aliases from session/set_config_option wire values.
selection_summary explicitly lists quick_models raw keys at acp/mod.rs4680-4692; commands.rs and the advertised available command describe /model [alias|default].
The new reserved_prefix_aliases_get_unique_wire_values_that_round_trip test exercises parse_model(wire_value(alias)) only, bypassing this real slash-command caller.
findings.fix: Give the slash-command entry point raw-alias parsing/encoding while keeping the protocol selector on canonical encoded IDs, or consistently display and document the encoded command operand. Ensure a displayed selection cannot route to another configured model.
acceptance_tests: Configure default, alias:default and alias:fast with different routes, obtain /model summary, then invoke the displayed aliases through PromptRequest slash commands and assert their exact configured routes. Keep the selector wire-ID round-trip test.

original_fix_validation.assessment: The originally identified context-relief seams are corrected in source. AnyAgent carries Arc<HeadlessBudgetCarry> into spawned interactive runner setup; every inspected TUI main/goal/loop start initializes a fresh carry, compact_and_respawn reuses it, begin_segment folds per-segment totals and subtracts them, and child relief passes max_turns-run.turns. Separately bounded one-turn tool-free summary exception is explicit. New tests cover runner-level remainder/token checks and child remainder/no-remaining-turn cases. The remaining SubagentStop sibling bypass is reported separately; no live App budget-respawn execution was performed here.

Original byte-only trigger veto is corrected: planner accepts byte_pressure, no-prefix and failed byte compaction install a futility floor, and a TUI handler integration test proves low-local-token byte pressure reaches the scripted summarizer and unchanged second pass avoids re-spend. Test uses text with a lowered byte threshold rather than literal images; existing Session image-floor tests cover image arithmetic. Ordinary real token-boundary bypass remains as runtime-rereview-1.

Original repeated-id misattribution is corrected: one ordered traversal pairs calls/results before reverse newest-path selection; non-read calls occupy pairing slots and ambiguous simultaneous duplicate ids are discarded rather than guessed. Added tests include successful+failed reused-id reads, both successful reads, non-read reuse and actual headless persistence. Source review found no further concrete pairing bug in valid transcript ordering.

SubagentStop coverage tests dispatch and saturated post-hoc merging independently, not task max_turns across the actual hook continuation branch.

Original interactive cap tests exercise two spawned runner segments and synthetic prior token publication rather than the full App summarization/respawn path. Inspection found carry wiring at all enumerated TUI spawn sites, but end-to-end token/turn-cap evidence remains limited.

findings.title: Initial Gemini command credentials still bypass query encoding and can lose renewal ownership
findings.origin: Adjacent remaining defect; predates this corrective diff. This is not a regression introduced by the xorxl.9 fix.
findings.scenario: A custom Gemini-compatible gateway uses a command-issued token containing a reserved query character. These characters are accepted by credential_from_output and are explicitly covered by the existing reserved-character encoding contract. The SDK constructs its initial request using that token directly in the key query field.
evidence: GeminiExt::build_uri formats self.api_key directly into the URL for both normal and streaming requests; it does not encode the query value.

CommandCredential::apply rewrites a query only when candidates does not contain current. Therefore a current construction-time token with a plus sign bypasses with_query_key and remains raw on the wire, where normal query decoding changes its value.

An ampersand in that initial token is worse: query_key splits the raw query at ampersands, so ownership sees only a prefix; apply returns None and the request loses the credential renewal/resend path as well as transmitting the wrong token.

query_key_rewrite_percent_encodes_reserved_characters tests with_query_key directly. gemini_query_string_key_is_refreshed_and_renewed_on_401 uses safe construction/rotation tokens, so neither exercises the initial SDK-built reserved-character token.
findings.mitigation: Encode the credential when the SDK initially builds the URL, or use Gemini header authentication so the full original token is never parsed out of an already ambiguous raw query. Canonicalizing only stale query credentials is insufficient.
regression_test_acceptance: Construct an actual custom Gemini SDK client once with a command helper whose first token contains reserved query characters; loopback assertions verify that both streaming and non-streaming requests contain exactly the original token after normal query decoding, with no unintended parameters.
Include initial plus, ampersand, percent, hash and space cases. Exercise a 401 followed by rotation and prove ownership/renewal remains attached.
Preserve the existing multi-rotation coverage and confirm safe tokens and unrelated query parameters remain unchanged.
findings.validation: Static call-path and indexed implementation review. No credential command, live provider request, exploit, or new proof-of-concept was executed.

findings.title: Keep MCP cancellation and EOF handling live while stdout is backpressured
findings.scenario: Start a silent long-running run, then let a ping/finished-run reply fill the MCP stdout pipe while the client stops reading. Close stdin or send notifications/cancelled. The dispatch task is stuck awaiting write_message and cannot receive the queued EOF/cancel; active model/tool work keeps running until its independent run timeout. The new EOF branch can also block flushing queued replies before the cancellation teardown.
evidence: serve awaits write_message inside its dispatch select arms (1127,1169); write_message uses unbounded output.write_all and flush awaits at1193-1194. The reader task can enqueue EOF/cancel, but the dispatch task cannot poll line_rx while blocked in a write.

The new EOF handler itself flushes all reply_rx entries through the same unbounded await before return (1081-1082). Active runs are cancelled only after this enclosing async block returns, at1179-1182.
The new stdin_eof_retires_a_silent_running_call_and_its_process_group test keeps stdout empty, so it proves idle EOF but not EOF/cancellation during a response write.

A deterministic source-level probe for the existing tests module is saved at /private/tmp/mini-agent-rereview-mcp-backpressure-probe.rs. It uses a one-byte output duplex, starts the existing shell fixture, confirms a ping response entered write_message by reading its first byte, then leaves stdout unread and closes stdin. Root may run it with coordinated Cargo; no Rust probe execution is claimed by this subagent.

Root independently executed the supplied current-source backpressure regression probe and observed retired=false, child_live=true; the blocked server was then aborted for cleanup. This confirms the concrete failure, beyond static path analysis.
findings.fix: Decouple/bound the output writer so transport retirement and notifications/cancelled can run while output is stalled; cancel and join active runs before any EOF reply drain, and bound that drain.
acceptance_tests: Run the supplied fixture and assert EOF retires serve and the whole child tree despite an open, unread stdout stream. Repeat using notifications/cancelled while a reply is blocked, and cover a large completed reply queued alongside an active run.
findings.validation: Root independently reproduced: retired=false child_live=true; cleanup completed.

findings.title: Own Windows helper and run descendants instead of killing only the direct process
findings.scenario: On Windows, an opted-in unsandboxed headersHelper launches a credential subprocess and waits. Cancel the MCP connect/reconnect or let the helper time out. The helper is killed, but the subprocess survives. The MCP server run process has the same direct-child-only ownership when a run is cancelled/retired.
evidence: The new GroupKillOnDrop has an empty Drop implementation outside Unix: its only action is under #[cfg(unix)] at headers_helper.rs87-90. command.process_group(0) is Unix-only too.

An unsandboxed helper comes from stdio_command as a plain tokio Command (client.rs1612-1618), then uses .kill_on_drop(true) and spawn_guarded (headers_helper.rs127-131). process_creation::spawn_tokio_once and TokioCommandCreationExt only acquire the creation lock and call TokioCommand::spawn; they never attach a Job Object.
The ordinary helper timeout/completion cleanup uses child.start_kill on non-Unix at headers_helper.rs156-158, so even waiting for the internal deadline does not terminate descendants.

server.rs run_prompt likewise launches a plain tokio Child with kill_on_drop, and its group guard is Unix-only. kill_tree on non-Unix calls only child.start_kill. Thus the new EOF teardown does not establish descendant retirement on Windows.

The repository already has owned_workspace_service_tree in sandbox.rs834-841, which wraps Windows workspace services in JobObject; these two paths bypass it. All new helper and MCP EOF fixtures are cfg(unix), leaving the platform branch unproved.
findings.fix: Use a Windows kill-on-close Job/owned process-tree wrapper for the helper and the MCP server run, retained through normal completion, timeout, cancellation and future drop. Preserve the Unix group guard.
acceptance_tests: On native Windows, have a helper and an MCP run each start a child that records its pid, then test cancellation, EOF, timeout and dropped-future paths; both the direct and descendant processes must be gone. Test the default unsandboxed trusted helper path.
findings.limitation: No native Windows execution performed; the missing Job ownership and cfg branches are directly visible.

findings.title: Parse raw aliases separately from encoded IDs in the ACP /model command
findings.scenario: Configure a quick-model alias named alias:fast. /model lists that raw name and advertises /model [alias|default], but typing /model alias:fast now fails because the wire decoder strips the prefix. If both default and alias:default exist, typing the displayed alias:default instead selects the default alias/provider.
evidence: The new parse_model correctly strips exactly one reserved prefix and validates the canonical wire encoding (134-135), making the selector IDs injective.

The slash command passes its raw argument directly to set_model_override at acp/mod.rs4077, which calls the same parse_model at2213; no encoding step distinguishes literal command aliases from session/set_config_option wire values.
selection_summary explicitly lists quick_models raw keys at acp/mod.rs4680-4692; commands.rs and the advertised available command describe /model [alias|default].
The new reserved_prefix_aliases_get_unique_wire_values_that_round_trip test exercises parse_model(wire_value(alias)) only, bypassing this real slash-command caller.
findings.fix: Give the slash-command entry point raw-alias parsing/encoding while keeping the protocol selector on canonical encoded IDs, or consistently display and document the encoded command operand. Ensure a displayed selection cannot route to another configured model.
acceptance_tests: Configure default, alias:default and alias:fast with different routes, obtain /model summary, then invoke the displayed aliases through PromptRequest slash commands and assert their exact configured routes. Keep the selector wire-ID round-trip test.
